blocks.response_text: In the 34 kV [reported] collection system the voltage fell rapidly to 20 kV [reported]. Trying to hold full active power at that voltage overloaded each turbine on Hornsea 1B and 1C, and their overcurrent protection de-loaded them, as the industry standard protection does to avoid permanent damage. The de-load ran from 16:52:33:728 to 16:52:33:835 [reported], 107 ms [reported]; Hornsea 1A stayed in operation at 62 MW [reported].

provenance.quote: The de-load was caused by an unexpected wind farm control system response, due to an insufficiently damped electrical resonance in the sub-synchronous frequency range, which was triggered by the initial event.

blocks.response_text: Our report concludes that the de-load was caused by an unexpected wind farm control system response, due to an insufficiently damped electrical resonance in the sub-synchronous frequency range, which was triggered by the initial event.
